hero_intro: Welcome to the Brubru EFPIA Brief. Every weekday until 28 June, you receive a short read of what moved in EU pharma and health policy in the last 24 hours, plus a confirmation that Brubru is tracking your priority files and that the agent itself has been updated. Five items today, the first to set the cadence.

headlines.title: DG SANTE has published the analysis underpinning the Biotech Act, the formal backing document for the seven-pillar architecture and the 20.4 billion euro envelope
headlines.snippet: The Commission released the impact-assessment evidence behind the Biotech Act proposal (Regulation track plus the genetically-modified microorganisms companion Directive). The analysis confirms the seven pillars (strategic projects, access to funding, biosimilars, AI and data, novel health biotech products, biosecurity, internationalisation), the three new governance bodies (Steering Group, Support Network, Foresight Panel), and the financial envelope under the next MFF window. For EFPIA's biotech members and the SME pipeline, this is the operational baseline the file will now be amended against. Brubru notes the procedure is still TABLED at the European Parliament; no rapporteur has been formally appointed yet for procedure 2025/0406(COD).
headlines.ask: What does the DG SANTE analysis underpinning the Biotech Act contain, and what is the current EP procedural status?

headlines.title: EMA confirms its summer plenary calendar, the CHMP meets 22 to 25 June in Amsterdam with PRAC and COMP back to back
headlines.snippet: The CHMP plenary scheduled for 22 to 25 June 2026 at EMA headquarters (Domenico Scarlattilaan 6, 1083 HS Amsterdam) is the next opinion-setting window before the August written-procedure month. PRAC meets 8 to 11 June and COMP 16 to 18 June. Member companies with applications in the queue should pre-position their rapporteur and co-rapporteur engagement now. Brubru's My EU Calendar carries the full 2026 schedule for CHMP, PRAC, COMP, CAT, PDCO and HMPC, filterable by institution and committee.
headlines.ask: When does the EMA CHMP next meet, and what are the 2026 plenary dates?

headlines.title: Hungarian and Polish national medicines authorities got Commission extensions to maintain emergency action on specific medicinal products
headlines.source: Official Journal, Commission Implementing Decisions 2026/1182 (Hungary) and 2026/1104 (Poland), late May 2026
headlines.snippet: Two implementing decisions extending Member State emergency measures under Article 5(1) of Directive 2001/83/EC were published in the Official Journal in the last week. These extensions are a thin but important channel through which national authorities can keep specific products available outside the standard marketing-authorisation route during shortages or local need. EFPIA member companies operating in those regulatory environments should map the affected products against their own portfolios. Brubru can pull the consolidated text on request.
headlines.ask: What did the Commission Implementing Decisions 2026/1182 and 2026/1104 extend, and what is the legal basis under Directive 2001/83/EC?

headlines.title: DG SANTE Health Security Committee met on 24 May, the senior-level summary report is now public
headlines.source: DG SANTE Health Security Committee summary report, published Tuesday 26 May 2026
headlines.snippet: The senior-level committee that coordinates Member State and Commission action under Decision 1082/2013/EU on serious cross-border threats to health convened on 24 May. The summary report covers the standing items on preparedness, surveillance, and joint procurement, and is the institutional layer EFPIA's vaccines and antimicrobial members track for anticipated joint procurement signals. The same DG SANTE update window also flagged a PHEG Subgroup meeting on lifelong prevention (22 May).
headlines.ask: What did the EU Health Security Committee discuss on 24 May 2026, and how does Decision 1082/2013/EU shape joint procurement?

headlines.title: Brubru is also tracking the Critical Medicines Act, Tomislav Sokol stays SANT rapporteur and the trilogue deal is now provisional
headlines.snippet: The CMA procedure 2025/0102(COD) reached a provisional inter-institutional agreement on 11 and 12 May 2026 under the Cyprus Council Presidency. It is not yet adopted, legal-linguistic revision and formal adoption by both institutions still to come. The headline trilogue change worth carrying: the threshold of Member States needed to ask the Commission to procure on their behalf dropped from nine to five. Tomislav Sokol (EPP, Croatia) remains the SANT rapporteur, with Tiemo Wolken (S&D) and the full shadow team unchanged from the report tabled in December.
headlines.ask: What is the current status of the Critical Medicines Act trilogue, and what changed in the joint-procurement threshold?
